key_logic_flow: OmniRoute 是一个开源 AI 路由器，聚合 40+ 供应商池/500+ 模型的免费层数据，通过单一 OpenAI 兼容端点提供统一接入。
该工具支持 17 种路由策略（priority、round-robin、cost-optimized、fusion 等）和 4 层自动故障转移（订阅→API Key→廉价→免费），确保提供商故障时零停机。
RTK + Caveman 堆叠压缩技术可减少 15-95% 的 token 消耗，工具密集型会话平均约 89%，有效降低使用成本。
OmniRoute 兼容 16+ 编码代理工具（Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Cline、Copilot、Antigravity 等），通过单套配置即可接入所有工具。
项目内置 MCP 服务器（87 个工具）、A2A 代理协议、TLS 指纹隐身、电路断路器、内存系统和护栏等生产级功能。
项目宣称每月可提供约 16 亿免费 token（按共享池去重后的真实计数），首次注册还可获得额外积分。

description: Instatic is a modern self-hosted visual CMS - get it running in 1 minute Instatic Own your site. Love building it. A self-hosted CMS where the visual editor, content engine, and publisher all live in one Bun server — and the pages it ships are clean enough to read in view-source. One-Click Deploy · Quick Start · Docs · Plugins · Roadmap Watch the introductory video about Instatic on YouTube. A modern website usually means assembling a stack: a headless CMS, a framework, a host, a form service, an analytics vendor, an image CDN — each with its own bill, dashboard, and 2 a.m. outage. Instatic is the opposite bet. One Bun server holds the whole thing — the canvas editor, the content engine, media, auth, forms, plugins, and the publisher — and you run it wherever you like, backed by SQLite or Postgres. What comes out the other end is the part most builders quietly compromise on: plain semantic HTML and compact CSS, with none of the editor's machinery left behind in the page. No framework runtime, no builder attributes, no div soup. The site loads like a static file because, most of the time, it is one. MIT. Self-hosted. Yours. Deploy in one click Railway is the fastest way to get Instatic live. Pick a template, hit the button, wait about two minutes. That's it. It generates the secret keys, attaches the storage volume, and sets up the health checks on its own. You never open a terminal. One minute to live. Unedited. Provider Database Best for Deploy Railway · Recommended SQLite A single site — blog, portfolio, small business Deploy → Railway Postgres Multiple authors, managed backups, room to grow Deploy → Render — — Coming soon Fly.io — — Coming soon DigitalOcean — — Coming soon SQLite is the right default for most sites. Reach for Postgres when you've got a team of authors or want managed database backups. Updating is just a redeploy When a new Instatic version is available, update by redeploying the latest image. Your database and uploads stay on the attached storage, so the app container can be replaced without rebuilding the site from scratch. Prefer your own hardware? Instatic is a single Docker image: INSTATIC_IMAGE=ghcr.io/corebunch/instatic:latest docker compose -f compose.prod.yml -f compose.sqlite.yml up -d Full guides for VPS, Postgres, HTTPS with Caddy, Render, and backups are in docs/deployment. One tool, the whole life of a site Most tools do one job and hand you off for the rest. You design in one place, build in another, keep content somewhere else, then bolt analytics on from a fourth. Instatic does all of it. Here's what's actually in the box. 🎨 Design The editor is a real canvas, not a form with a preview pane stapled to it. You put several breakpoint frames side by side and edit them together. Change the desktop and the mobile frame reacts in the same view. When you'd rather work on the real thing, flip to live mode and edit a single full-size page in place. The part nobody else has: Core Framework is built in. It's the design-token engine thousands of WordPress pros already use every day, and here it's a core system, not a plugin you install and pray over. Color tokens that generate their own shade scale. Define one brand color, get the full set of tuned tints and shades automatically. Type scales that are fluid and mathematical. One ramp that scales with the viewport, instead of forty hand-picked font sizes you have to keep in sync. Spacing scales so every page and every breakpoint keeps the same rhythm. A utility-class generator that emits locked, generated classes into one small framework.css. No bloat, no duplicate rules, nothing you didn't ask for. Your whole design system lives as data. Change one token and every page that uses it updates. 🧱 Build Modules are the building blocks: containers, text, images, buttons, video, lists, links, SVG, forms. Drag them onto the canvas and nest them however you want. Visual Components are reusable pieces with typed parameters and named slots. A parameter can be a string, number, boolean, color, image, URL, rich text, an enum, or a whole slot of content. Edit the component once and every instance on the site updates. Components that would reference themselves are blocked before they happen, so nothing eats its own tail. Templates handle the shared chrome. One layout for the whole site, separate layouts per post type, and a real 404 page you design yourself. Content flows into an outlet, so a header and footer get written once and wrap everything. Loops repeat a layout over a collection: your posts, your pages, your media, or anything a plugin exposes as a source. Give a loop a couple of variants and it alternates between them as it goes. Good for post lists, product grids, galleries. Forms that belong to your CMS. Build a form out of semantic fields and the submissions land in your own data tables. Instatic can read the fields you placed and create the matching table for you. No third-party form service, no embed, no monthly fee for a contact form. An AI agent that actually edits the page. Describe what you want and it builds it on the canvas as real, editable nodes, not a screenshot or a wall of code. It writes semantic HTML for structure and CSS for style, through the same import pipeline you use when you paste markup. 28 tools under the hood. Bring your own model: Claude, OpenAI, OpenRouter, or local Ollama. Your key, your model, your bill. Imports that hold up. Paste raw HTML and get editable nodes. Or drop a whole static site — HTML, CSS, images, fonts — and Super Import turns it into pages, style rules, design tokens, and media. Every conflict is shown to you before anything is written, and the entire import is a single undo. 🗂 Manage One content model under everything. Pages, posts, components, custom collections, and any structured table you invent all live in the same store: data_tables and data_rows. There's no special-cased "pages" table hiding in a corner. Schemas, raw rows, imports, exports, and form submissions all sit in one consistent place. A Data workspace where you design your own collections. At /admin/data you create custom post types and custom data tables with their own fields, then work the rows in a spreadsheet-style grid: search, sort, filter, bulk publish, bulk export. Custom post types come with a real editorial workflow — draft, scheduled, published — and version history on the published copy. Plain data tables are simple grids you can point at anything: the submissions from a form, a product catalog, a lightweight CRM, a list of testimonials. And every table you build is a content source a loop can render. Define a "Team" table once, loop it onto your about page, done. A content workspace for writing. A focused surface for posts and collections, plus live mode so authors edit inside the real design of the site instead of a gray textarea. A media workspace that works like a file manager. Folders and smart folders, bulk operations, usage tracking so you know where a file is actually used, replacement workflows, and pluggable storage adapters when you outgrow local disk. Access control that's real, not decorative. Roles built from 36 capabilities, token-based sessions, TOTP two-factor with secrets encrypted at rest, account lockout with backoff after repeated failures, and step-up prompts before the dangerous stuff like deleting a user or signing out every device. ⌘K for everything. A fuzzy command palette over the whole admin. Jump anywhere, do anything, without touching the mouse. Drafts stay drafts. Unpublished edits never leak to a visitor. What you didn't publish, they don't see. 📊 Analyze A dashboard you arrange yourself. A 12-column grid of tile widgets you can drag, resize, and rearrange. Add the ones you care about in customize mode, and the layout saves per user. Plugins can ship their own widgets into the same grid. An audit log that doesn't forget. Every meaningful admin action writes a row: logins, content changes, role edits, plugin lifecycle. It's append-only, so it's a real record of who did what and when, not something anyone can quietly rewrite. Form data that's yours. Submissions sit in your own tables. Query them, export them, build on them. No vendor in the middle. This is the youngest pillar, and the one we're pushing hardest right now. First-party, privacy-respecting analytics are next. See the roadmap. 🔌 Extend --> Every CMS has plugins. The difference here is where they run. An Instatic plugin is a zip package with a manifest, and it runs inside a QuickJS-WASM sandbox. No filesystem. No environment variables. No network at all, unless the site owner grants it, one host at a time. A plugin can't read your secrets or phone home, because the sandbox never hands it the door. The classic "a plugin took down my site and emailed the database to a stranger" story doesn't run here. Inside that sandbox the SDK is genuinely capable. A plugin can add: HTTP routes and its own admin pages Storage and scheduled background jobs Loop data sources, so your content loops can pull from anywhere Canvas modules — new blocks that show up in the editor Media storage adapters and frontend assets Lifecycle hooks across install, activation, and beyond Start with the plugin system docs and the template plugin. Fast because there's almost nothing to load --> A published Instatic page is mostly just a file sitting on disk. No framework to boot, no hydration step, no database round-trip on the common path. The browser pulls down semantic HTML and a compact stylesheet, and it's done. There's barely anything between the visitor and the content, so the pages feel instant. That speed isn't a setting you tune. It falls out of how publishing works, in three layers you never have to think about: Static pages are baked straight to disk when you publish and swapped in atomically. Visitors are served a file, not a render. Routes that genuinely change hit an in-memory cache that's wiped wholesale on every publish, so nobody ever sees a stale page. The few truly per-visitor parts are detected automatically and lazy-loaded by a runtime that weighs about 0.7 kB. Smaller than this paragraph. What comes out the other end is plain HTML and compact CSS, all the way down. Nothing from the editor rides along: no React on your public pages, no editor runtime, no framework in the markup. And because it's just HTML and CSS, nothing holds your site hostage — you can read it, host it anywhere, or take it and leave. Full design: the publisher. Quick start You need Bun. Nothing else. The default dev setup runs on SQLite, so there are no extra services to stand up. git clone https://github.com/corebunch/instatic.git cd instatic bun install bun run dev Open http://localhost:5173. The first visit walks you through creating your site and your owner account. Want to see it the way it actually ships? bun run start builds the admin and serves it from the Bun server at http://localhost:3001/admin. Backups, in one sentence: back up the database (a Postgres dump or the SQLite file) and the uploads folder, and you've backed up the whole site — details. Who's behind this We're the team behind Motion.page and Core Framework — tools that thousands of people use to build websites for a living, mostly in the WordPress world. We spent years making other platforms more bearable. At some point the obvious question wouldn't go away: what if the thing underneath was just right to begin with? No legacy to work around, no markup we're not allowed to touch, no business model that depends on keeping your site where we can see it. So we built Instatic. And we brought Core Framework along, wired in as a core system, so the color shades, type scales, spacing, and utility classes our users already rely on are part of the product — not an add-on you install and hope for the best. Early, on purpose Here's the honest part: this is version 0.0.x. Everything above — the canvas, Core Framework, the universal content model, the sandboxed plugins, the AI agent, forms, loops, templates, media, MFA, the audit log, one-click deploy, the clean publisher — is the starting line, not the finish. What's coming: Real analytics. First-party and privacy-respecting, to round out the Analyze pillar. A bigger module and plugin ecosystem. More first-party blocks, more SDK surface, more examples to copy from. A sharper AI agent. More tools, deeper awareness of your actual site. Everything tighter. We're pre-1.0 on purpose. It's the cheapest time to throw out bad ideas and keep the architecture clean. APIs and workflows can still shift before 1.0. If that makes you nervous, wait for 1.0 — no hard feelings. If you'd rather help shape what site ownership looks like for the next twenty years, now's the good seat. For developers One Bun server. A React admin built with Vite. A publisher that emits pages you'd be happy to have written yourself. Runtime Bun, for both server and tooling Language TypeScript everywhere Admin app React 19 (React Compiler on), Vite, Zustand + Mutative, CodeMirror, dnd-kit Server Bun.serve with a hand-written router Database SQLite or Postgres — one DbClient interface, picked by DATABASE_URL Validation TypeBox at every untyped boundary; schemas are the source of truth Plugins QuickJS-WASM sandbox, owner-granted permissions AI Provider-agnostic drivers over raw HTTP/SSE, no vendor SDKs Output Semantic HTML, compact CSS, baked static files plus auto-detected dynamic holes The codebase is opinionated, and the opinions are enforced in code. Architectural rules live in src/__tests__/architecture/ as actual tests, so the structure that keeps the output clean can't quietly rot. bun run build # tsc -b && vite build bun test bun run lint Dig in: docs index · architecture · editor · server · publisher · plugin system Thanks Instatic's interface uses Pixelarticons by Gerrit Halfmann. Thanks to Gerrit for a genuinely distinctive icon set, and for kindly letting us use it in an open-source project. License MIT. See LICENSE. No tiers, no open-core asterisks, no "contact sales."
tldr: CoreBunch 发布自托管 CMS Instatic，整合编辑、内容与发布于单一 Bun 服务器
objective_summary: CoreBunch 团队推出 Instatic，一个 MIT 开源的自托管 CMS。它将可视化编辑器、内容引擎、媒体管理、表单和发布功能整合在单一 Bun 服务器中，支持 SQLite 或 Postgres 数据库，可通过 Docker 或一键部署到 Railway 等平台。
key_logic_flow: Instatic 是一个自托管的 CMS，将可视化编辑器、内容引擎和发布器整合在单一的 Bun 服务器中。
项目采用 MIT 开源协议，支持 SQLite（默认）或 Postgres 数据库，可通过 Docker 或一键部署到 Railway 等平台。
内置 Core Framework 设计令牌引擎，可自动生成颜色色阶、流体文字比例和间距体系，所有设计系统以数据形式存储。
插件系统运行在 QuickJS-WASM 沙盒中，默认无文件系统和网络访问权限，需站点所有者逐主机授权。
发布的页面生成纯语义 HTML 和紧凑 CSS 静态文件，无框架运行时或编辑器残留负载。
内置 AI 编辑器代理，支持 Claude、OpenAI、OpenRouter 或本地 Ollama 模型，可在画布上直接生成可编辑节点。

impact_score.reason: Instatic 是一个设计精良的自托管 CMS 发布，其核心创新在于将可视化编辑器、内容引擎和发布器整合到单一 Bun 服务器中，并通过 Core Framework 设计令牌引擎实现设计系统数据化。但这本质上是 CMS 领域的产品发布，而非 AI 行业范式转移。AI 编辑器代理（支持 Claude/Ollama 等）是亮点但非核心突破，QuickJS-WASM 沙盒插件系统在安全架构上有新意。在自托管 CMS 赛道（WordPress、Strapi、TinaCMS 等）中是一个有力的新竞争者，但尚未达到改变行业格局的程度。综合评定为 5.0 分——重要的产品发布，局部竞争格局变化，但非全行业冲击。

developer_sentiment.primary_focus: Bun 单服务架构能否在生产环境中替代传统 CMS 堆栈的可靠性与生态成熟度

hype_assessment.reason: 文章整体较为务实，列出了具体的功能清单和架构决策（Bun、SQLite/Postgres、QuickJS-WASM），但也存在一定的 PR 包装痕迹。例如 'the pages it ships are clean enough to read in view-source' 和 'the part most builders quietly compromise on' 属于典型的营销话术，暗示竞品存在妥协。'颠覆'、'革命性'等词汇未直接出现，但'无人做到的部分'（The part nobody else has）的表述有抬高自身之嫌。整体上干货与包装并存，属于中等炒作水平。

domain_disruption.technical_innovation: 将 Bun 运行时作为单一服务承载完整的 CMS 前后端（编辑器+内容引擎+发布器），并内置 Core Framework 设计令牌引擎实现颜色色阶/流体文字/间距体系的自动生成，设计系统以数据而非代码形式存储。插件系统运行在 QuickJS-WASM 沙盒中（默认无文件系统/网络权限），提供比传统插件模型更强的安全隔离。AI 编辑器代理可生成可编辑节点而非截图或代码片段，绕过常规的 'AI 写代码 → 粘贴 → 查看' 工作流。
domain_disruption.business_model: MIT 开源协议 + Docker 一键部署 + Railway/Render 等平台的模板化部署，无需 SaaS 订阅即可获得完整的 CMS 功能。内置表单处理消除了对第三方表单服务的依赖，降低了小型站点的月费成本。对 Motion.page 的 Core Framework 用户社区形成了从 WordPress 插件到自有 CMS 的生态迁移通路。

compound_value.reason: Instatic 在技术架构上有显著差异化：单一 Bun 服务器整合全栈（编辑器+内容引擎+发布器）、Core Framework 设计令牌引擎内置（已在 WordPress 生态有数千用户基础）、QuickJS-WASM 沙盒插件隔离、输出纯净语义 HTML/CSS 无框架运行时残留、AI 编辑器直接在画布生成可编辑节点而非代码片段。这些特性在自托管 CMS 领域具有长期积累潜力，尤其是 Core Framework 的存量用户迁移和设计系统数据化存储能形成一定的切换成本。但需清醒认识：CMS 市场极度拥挤（WordPress 生态霸权、Webflow/Framer 在视觉建站领域品牌强势、Strapi/Ghost 等开源竞品各有拥趸），MIT 开源协议下变现路径不明（目前仅靠部署平台 Railway 合作），Bun 生态仍在早期成熟度不足。中长期看，若 CoreBunch 能围绕插件市场、托管服务和 AI 功能建立订阅收入模型，有机会成为开发者自托管 CMS 赛道的差异化选手，但距离行业基石还有很长的验证期。

competitive_casualty: 传统 SaaS 建站平台
market_opportunities: 自由开发者和小型工作室可利用 Instatic 的全栈整合能力，为客户提供从设计到内容管理再到一键部署的打包服务，抽取代维费用而非依赖多个第三方 SaaS
WordPress 设计师群体可基于内置的 Core Framework 设计令牌引擎迁移到现代栈，用 Instatic 替代传统 WordPress + 页面构建器的组合，降低维护复杂度

risk_matrix.regulatory: 自托管模式将数据合规责任转移给部署者，但插件沙盒（QuickJS-WASM）默认限制文件系统和网络访问，降低了第三方插件带来的监管风险
risk_matrix.technological: Bun 运行时生态尚不成熟，相比 Node.js 存在长期维护和兼容性不确定性；QuickJS-WASM 沙盒的性能和插件丰富度有待验证；CMS 市场已有 WordPress、Strapi、Ghost 等成熟解决方案，用户迁移成本较高
risk_matrix.competitive: CMS 赛道极度拥挤，大型开源 CMS 拥有庞大的插件生态和社区积累，Instatic 作为新生项目在品牌认知、社区规模和第三方集成方面面临显著劣势
risk_matrix.ethical: 内置 AI 编辑器代理支持多种模型，若用户使用未经充分安全对齐的开源模型（如本地 Ollama），可能生成不当内容；自托管场景下内容审核责任完全由站点所有者承担

tldr: Google 发布 agents-cli：为 AI 编程助手提供 CLI 和技能，用于在 Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
objective_summary: Google 发布了 agents-cli，这是一个面向 AI 编程助手（如 Claude Code、Codex）的 CLI 工具和技能套件，提供 scaffold、eval、deploy、publish 等命令，用于在 Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform 上基于
key_logic_flow: Google 发布了 agents-cli，这是一个为 AI 编程助手提供 CLI 命令和技能的开发工具，而非独立编码助手。
agents-cli 支持与 Antigravity CLI、Claude Code、Codex 等多种编码助手协同工作，技能覆盖开发周期、ADK 代码、脚手架、评估、部署、发布和可观测性七个维度。
核心命令包括 scaffold（创建/增强/升级项目）、eval（生成/评分/对比/分析评估结果）、deploy（部署到 Google Cloud）和 publish（注册到 Gemini Enterprise）。
本地开发不需要 Google Cloud，可使用 AI Studio API Key；部署和云功能需要 Google Cloud 环境。
agents-cli 也支持独立使用 CLI 模式，无需搭配编码助手，所有命令均可直接在终端运行。

impact_score.reason: agents-cli 是 Google 为 Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform 发布的开发者工具套件，而非独立编码助手。它提供了 scaffold、eval、deploy、publish 等命令和技能（Skill），让 Claude Code、Codex 等第三方编码助手能够端到端构建和部署 ADK 智能体。这在战略层面值得关注——Google 主动拥抱编码助手生态，降低了开发者使用 Google Cloud Agent Platform 的门槛。但本质上它是现有基础设施（ADK + Google Cloud）的编排层，没有引入新的模型架构或训练范式。对于 Google Cloud 生态内开发者有显著价值，对行业整体格局影响有限。综合评分 5.8，属于重要产品发布，改变局部的 Google Cloud 智能体开发生态竞争格局。

developer_sentiment.primary_focus: Google Cloud 生态锁定 vs 与第三方编码助手的良好集成体验

hype_assessment.reason: 文章本身是 GitHub README，语言朴实、技术细节具体。没有出现'颠覆性''革命性'等 PR 滥用词汇，而是明确说明了 agents-cli 不是独立编码助手（'not a coding agent itself'），清楚列出了限制条件（本地开发不需要 Google Cloud，部署需要）、技能边界和依赖关系。属于实打实的开发者工具发布，水分很低。

domain_disruption.technical_innovation: 无本质技术突破。agents-cli 的核心创新在于将 Google Cloud Agent Platform 的能力打包为标准化 Skill（MCP 格式），使得第三方编码助手能够通过自然语言指令直接编排 ADK 框架的完整开发生命周期。这种'CLI + Skill 套件'的模式本身不是新技术，而是对现有基础设施的开发者体验做了系统化的集成编排。
domain_disruption.business_model: 强化了 Google Cloud 在 Agent Platform 领域的生态绑定策略。通过降低第三方编码助手（而非 Google 自家产品）部署到 Google Cloud 的门槛，Google 意在争夺 AI 代理部署工作负载的云市场份额。这与竞争对手（AWS、Azure）的代理平台形成直接竞争，核心差异化在于对编码助手生态的开放程度。

compound_value.reason: 长期复利需分两层看。第一层，agents-cli 本身是 Google Cloud 的开发者锁定工具（vendor lock-in），通过开源+多编码助手兼容策略降低 Agent 构建门槛，将开发者引入 Gemini Enterprise + Google Cloud 生态。其复利效应取决于 Agent 工作负载在云端的迁移速度——一旦开发者在 agents-cli 上完成 scaffold→eval→deploy 全流程，迁移成本就形成了粘性，且会拉动 GCP 资源消耗（Cloud Run、GKE、BigQuery）。第二层，工具本身是开源的、standalone 可用，如果 Google 持续投入社区治理，有机会成为 Agent 开发工具链的事实标准之一，但这需要与 LangChain、LlamaIndex 等现有生态竞争。风险点在于：(1) agents-cli 目前绑定 ADK 和 Google Cloud，跨平台兼容性有限；(2) 如果 Agent 开发范式未来向 MCP 等标准化协议收敛，专属工具的价值可能被稀释；(3) 大模型调用层（AI Studio API Key）和云部署层之间的依赖关系意味着低成本入门但高成本生产，可能引发开发者反感。综合评估：有潜力成为 GCP 生态内的 Agent 开发基础设施，但独立于 Google Cloud 的长期价值存疑，需持续观察社区采纳和跨平台策略。

competitive_casualty: 中小型 Agent 框架厂商
market_opportunities: 咨询公司和服务商可围绕 agents-cli 提供企业级 Agent 构建、评估和部署的端到端咨询服务，利用该工具降低交付成本并锁定 Google Cloud 生态客户
独立开发者或初创团队可开发 agents-cli 的垂直行业技能包（如金融合规审计 Agent、医疗诊断 Agent 的脚手架与评估模板），抢占 Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform 的应用生态位
借鉴 agents-cli 的开放技能模式，可开发跨云 Agent 开发工具链——为 AWS Bedrock 或 Azure AI 构建类似的 CLI+技能套件，满足多云/混合云企业的统一开发体验需求

title: facebook/astryx
description: An open source design system that's fully customizable and agent readyAstryx An open source design system that's fully customizable and built for how we build now — by people and the agents working alongside them. Currently in Beta · Built on React and StyleX Overview Astryx is an open source design system that grew inside Meta over the last eight years, where it became the most-used and largest design system in the company — powering 13,000+ apps and shaped by the engineers, designers, and product teams who depend on it every day. It ships 150+ accessible components, brand-level theming, dark mode, ready-to-ship templates, and a CLI as one cohesive system. You import pre-built CSS and use typed React components — no build plugin, no styling library to adopt — and both people and AI assistants build with the same tooling. What makes Astryx different: Open internals. Components are built to be composed at any level, not locked behind a closed top-level API. The building blocks you'd reach for are exported directly, and when you need to go deeper, swizzle ejects a component's full source into your project to own. No styling lock-in. Astryx authors its styles with StyleX, but that's invisible to consumers. Override with className using Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS — whatever your project already uses. Customize without wrapping. A theme is a set of CSS custom property overrides, so a designer can make Astryx unmistakably theirs without forking or wrapping component source. Built for people and agents. The API, docs, and CLI are designed together so a person and an AI assistant build the same way, from the same reference. Getting Started Install Astryx and a theme: # npm npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli # pnpm pnpm add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral pnpm add -D @astryxdesign/cli # yarn yarn add @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral yarn add -D @astryxdesign/cli The simplest setup is a few CSS imports plus a theme provider — no build plugin, no PostCSS or Babel config. See the @astryxdesign/core README for the full guide (Next.js, Tailwind, Vite, and CDN). For reliable CLI access, add a script to your package.json: "scripts": { "astryx": "node node_modules/@astryxdesign/cli/bin/astryx.mjs" } Then use it as npm run astryx -- component --list. This avoids path errors when AI assistants or new developers invoke the CLI directly. Packages Package Description README @astryxdesign/core Components, theme system, and utilities README @astryxdesign/cli CLI tooling: component docs, templates, scaffolding, themes, and codemods README @astryxdesign/build Build plugins for StyleX source builds README @astryxdesign/theme-* Seven ready-made, fully customizable themes (neutral, butter, chocolate, matcha, stone, gothic, y2k) README @astryxdesign/lab (experimental components) and @astryxdesign/vega (Vega/Vega-Lite chart wrapper) are used internally for Storybook and the sandbox; they are not yet published to npm. Principles These are the promises Astryx makes to the people building on it. Guidance over enforcement. Components give you capability rather than guardrails that fight you. Design opinions live in docs and examples — if you pass a value, the component renders it. Strong, documented conventions. Every component follows the same naming, prop, and composition rules, and every one is thoroughly documented — so once you've learned a few, the rest feel familiar, and both people and AI can predict how an unfamiliar component behaves. One system for humans and AI. The API, conventions, docs, and CLI are designed together so people and AI assistants build the same way. Every change that made Astryx easier for AI made it easier for people too. Earned by measurement. We test conventions rather than assert them, hold the results loosely, and revisit them when a new situation proves them wrong. Architecture Foundations The building blocks for visually cohesive and accessible interfaces: typography, color, layout, and accessibility. Components A library of 150+ reusable UI building blocks with full TypeScript support. Patterns Battle-tested design solutions for common interactions and workflows: table pages, detail page layouts, form wizards, navigation patterns, data entry flows. Project Structure Directory Purpose apps/ Example apps, the docsite, and Storybook packages/ Published packages: core, cli, build, themes internal/ Internal tooling: test utilities, eslint plugin, vibe tests Contributing We welcome contributions! See CONTRIBUTING.md for the full guide. Quick start for contributors: this repo uses pnpm 10 via Corepack. Enable it once and the right pnpm version installs automatically: corepack enable pnpm install License MIT

impact_score.reason: Meta 开源内部设计系统 Astryx 对前端/设计系统领域有重要影响，但并非范式级转变。其差异化在于：无样式锁定（StyleX 内部编写但消费者可用任意 CSS）、swizzle 组件源码弹出机制、以及同时面向人类和 AI 助手的工具链设计。然而，设计系统赛道已有 Material UI、Radix、Shadcn/ui、Ant Design 等成熟竞品，Astryx 的差异化虽值得关注但不足以颠覆现有格局。MIT 协议和 Meta 背书会吸引早期采用者，但生态迁移成本高，短期影响有限。

developer_sentiment.primary_focus: 无样式锁定架构允许在 Astryx 上使用 Tailwind/CSS Modules 等已有方案，以及面向 AI 代理设计的 CLI 和文档工具链

hype_assessment.reason: 文章表述务实，未使用'颠覆性''革命性'等 PR 滥用词汇。Astryx 的定位是 Meta 内部八年实战验证后的开源释放，具备 13,000+ 应用的工程背书。功能描述具体（150+ 组件、7 个主题包、swizzle 机制），信息真实可验证，不存在概念炒作。

domain_disruption.technical_innovation: 采用 StyleX 编写内部样式但对消费者透明的无样式锁定架构，通过 className 属性兼容 Tailwind/CSS Modules/纯 CSS；swizzle 机制允许将组件源码弹出到项目中进行完全控制；主题系统基于 CSS 自定义属性覆盖，设计师无需 fork 或包裹组件即可自定义外观；工具链同时为人类和 AI 代理设计，确保两者使用相同的 API、文档和 CLI。
domain_disruption.business_model: 以 MIT 协议彻底开源，无任何商业限制，通过社区贡献和生态建设增强 Meta 在前端/设计工具领域的技术领导力。这与 Meta 的 React、StyleX、Jest 等开源策略一脉相承——通过底层基础设施开源来吸引人才和塑造行业标准，而非直接变现。

compound_value.reason: Astryx 是 Meta 内部验证八年后开源的高质量设计系统，具备150+组件、主题系统和AI友好文档等扎实特性。但从VC视角看，MIT协议下不存在直接变现路径，UI组件库赛道拥挤（Material UI、Ant Design、Radix、Shadcn等均已建立社区壁垒），用户切换成本极低，无法形成网络效应或数据飞轮。'AI友好设计'是其最大差异化——API和文档同时面向人类和AI代理，但这属于品类内的功能增强而非品类重构，不足以创造独立商业价值。Meta开源的战略意图更偏向开发者生态影响力建设和人才吸引，而非追求财务回报。这是一个'好产品但非好投资'的典型标的——使用价值高但资本价值有限。

tldr: herdr：基于 Rust 的 AI 编码代理终端多路复用器，支持状态监控与持久化会话。
objective_summary: ogulcancelik 发布了 herdr v0.4.0，一个基于 Rust 的终端多路复用工具，为每个 AI 编码代理提供独立真实终端视图，支持阻塞/工作中/完成/空闲状态监控、工作区管理、持久化会话和 SSH 远程连接，采用 AGPL-3.0 与商业双许可证。
key_logic_flow: herdr 是一个专为 AI 编码代理构建的终端多路复用器，为每个代理提供独立的真实终端视图，而非应用的模拟终端。
侧边栏自动检测代理状态，将每个代理归为阻塞（红色）、工作中（黄色）、完成（蓝色）或空闲（绿色），无需额外钩子配置。
支持工作区、标签页和面板的拖拽管理，内置鼠标原生交互和键盘快捷键（ctrl+b 前缀模型）。
后台服务器确保持久化运行，关闭笔记本后代理不会终止，可通过其他终端或手机 SSH 重新连接。
单个约 10MB 的 Rust 二进制文件，无外部依赖，支持 Linux 和 macOS（Windows beta），可通过 curl、Homebrew、mise、Nix 安装。
提供本地 Unix Socket API 和 CLI，代理可通过 npx skills 安装可复用技能来创建工作区、分割面板、读取输出和订阅状态变化。

impact_score.reason: herdr 是首个专为 AI 编码代理设计的终端多路复用器，填补了 tmux/zellij 无法感知代理状态、而 GUI 代理管理器（如 Conductor、cmux）又缺乏持久化终端真实渲染的空白。随着 Claude Code、Cursor、Copilot CLI、Devin CLI 等 AI 编码代理的迅速普及，多代理并发会话管理成为开发者日益增长的痛点。herdr 以 10MB Rust 二进制文件提供了 'tmux 的持久性 + 代理状态感知' 的组合，且支持 SSH 远程重连和 Socket API 可编程接口。这是一个重要的开发者基础设施改进，但并未改变 AI 底层范式，属于生态补充型工具。评分 5.8，介于 '重要产品发布，改变局部竞争格局' 的偏低端。

developer_sentiment.primary_focus: 多代理并发会话的统一管理与状态实时监控

hype_assessment.reason: 文章语调务实，详细列出受支持的 18 种 AI 代理并诚实标注了未充分测试的代理，提供了与 tmux、GUI 管理器等的功能对比表，承认了竞争对手在代理状态展示方面的优势（'table stakes'）。没有使用 '颠覆'、'革命性' 等 PR 词汇，对自身定位清晰（'it's that, rebuilt for agents'），因此炒作指数低。

domain_disruption.technical_innovation: 为每个 AI 编码代理分配独立真实终端（非模拟终端），基于进程名匹配加终端输出启发式算法实现代理状态自动检测（阻塞/工作中/完成/空闲），无需额外钩子配置；后台服务器保证会话持久化，支持 SSH 客户端重连和跨设备断点续连；提供本地 Unix Socket API，代理可通过 npx skills 直接编排工作区创建、面板分割和状态订阅。
domain_disruption.business_model: AGPL-3.0 开源社区版 + 商业双许可证模式，与 tmux、Zellij 等开源项目形成差异化定位。随着 AI 编码代理成为主流开发范式，herdr 有潜力成为 AI 代理开发工作流中的基础设施层工具，可能催生围绕 Socket API 的插件生态和商业支持服务。

compound_value.reason: herdr 精准瞄准了 AI 编码代理生态中一个真实且日益尖锐的基础设施缺口：多代理终端的统一管理、状态感知与持久化。随着 Claude Code、Codex CLI、Copilot CLI、Devin 等编码代理工具快速普及，开发者需要在终端中同时运行和监控多个代理会话，传统 tmux 不具备代理感知能力，而 GUI 代理管理器（Conductor、cmux 等）存在平台锁定、非轻量、无法 SSH 等局限。herdr 的 Rust 单二进制（~10MB）、零依赖、AGPL+商业双许可、原生 SSH 远程重连、Unix Socket API 可编程性，使其具有成为 'AI 时代 tmux' 的潜力。然而该项目目前为个人开发者维护（v0.4.0），面临三个关键风险：（1）tmux/zellij 可能快速跟进加入代理感知功能；（2）主流代理平台（Anthropic、OpenAI、GitHub）可能内置类似多会话管理能力，挤压第三方工具生存空间；（3）单点故障风险（单一维护者）。长期复利取决于社区采用速度、集成深度以及与主要代理平台的关系演变，目前处于 '有潜力的细分基础设施种子期'，但距离 '3-5 年后行业基石'仍有较大不确定性。

market_opportunities: 开发者可基于 herdr 的 Socket API 构建自定义的 AI 编码代理编排与监控面板，实现多代理协作状态的可视化调度
DevOps 团队可利用 herdr 的持久化会话和 SSH 远程连接特性，在云端开发服务器上统一管理分布式 AI 编码代理集群
企业可将 herdr 集成到内部开发工具链中，通过其插件系统实现代理状态与 CI/CD 流水线、代码审查系统的联动
